So, I have been mulling a lot of thoughts over the past week. I was originally going to let this be a discussion piece among our moderator team, but ultimately I decided to put this out there for all to see. Consider this an unauthorized family meeting at The Dinner Table.

The Dinner Table: Past

For those who are unaware of the beginnings, here is a brief origin story, so that you may contextualize everything that follows. I am one of many readers of Wait But Why, which has a weekly-ish section called "Dinner Table," where a question is chosen for the readership to discuss. I enjoyed it, but I thirsted for it to occur more often, and I thirsted for the ability to submit my own questions. Voat seemed like a nice opportunity to see if this could be established. I never would have guessed that we would have grown to a few hundred subscribers. I expected a dozen or so people making a single post a couple of times a week. But during the first few days, @MrBlueSky expressed an interest in this subverse, and we began talking about development. At her urging, my original format was scrapped, we decided to be a lot more open to topics and format, and then divided responsibilities. I took on the CSS, and she handled public relations. Over a few weeks, we put forth a lot of effort to make this an attractive subverse where people could discuss pretty much anything on their mind without any drama. One of our most active members at the time, @FuzzyWords, hopped on board as our third moderator, and helped in cleaning up the CSS while also doing some PR on the side.

The Dinner Table: Present

During our beginnings, we had tried to establish the sort of tone that we wanted, even requesting feedback from the few people that were here originally. Most people seemed apathetic, or at least that was my interpretation based on the lack of response we were getting. So, I tried to make the rules very simple -- try to be civil, don't take things seriously, talk about whatever you want. I threw in an appropriated list of rules from the movie Fight Club to establish our theme, while also signaling the relaxed tone that I was going for.

I am sure many of you are familiar with the drama surrounding pompous-gate, so I won't go into that in detail. I just want to address the aftermath and what that means for us as a community. Even though my personal feelings on the subject of comment deletion are that it has its place, it seems that site-wide, majority of people are fundamentally opposed. If that's what people want, then I will support that. The incident did initiate a dialogue on the matter, and I am very glad that it did. Most people disagreed with a single comment being deleted, but simultaneously commended us for the handling of the situation. Myself and the person involved kindly apologized to one another, and we seem to have agreed that the interaction was a misunderstanding. Still, though, I want to discuss policy about the tone and rules at The Dinner Table. And this is where all of you come in!

The Dinner Table: Future

If you take a gander over at the sidebar, you will see a lot of different things. The first of which is a welcome message telling people what we are about. Over time, this seems to have evolved. Let's be honest, sometimes serious subjects come up at both the dinner table and at The Dinner Table. Do we need to comment upon that? Are we no longer just silly and frivolous? Do some of our topics have meaning? Personally, I think this takes highest priority of the amendments to the sidebar. Am I wrong?

In terms of our "Table Manners," my thoughts have been that there only needs to be one minor change. "Civil discourse is appreciated" is too suggestive. It does not command civil discussion, it merely recommends it. Originally, we did not want to chase people off. We wanted to be inviting. At this point, however, most people have expressed how much they enjoy the relaxed atmosphere of our community. So perhaps civil discourse is no longer appreciated? Should we state, "Be civil," or "Be respectful," in its stead? I still like the, "don't take things too seriously," because it seems to say that we discourage fighting, while also welcoming polite argument. Maybe that's just my perception? I also think our "Submission Rules" are fine. But if we have an "anything goes" mentality, then that should probably be reflected in the description of this community, as was stated before.

Here's something that really surprised me: people have interpreted our "Subverse Rules" pretty seriously. It's a pleasant surprise, but a surprise, nonetheless. It was supposed to bring about a sense of levity, but the comments that I have seen about them have really opened my eyes to the effect that they have had on our membership. Am I crazy? Do people like them as much as it seems?

Additionally, since our membership has grown, I also want to field any other ideas that may help to enhance this subverse. Over at v-askgoat, they have started doing their own "Question of the Week," which I thought was a fantastic idea. Are there things that we can also do to separate ourselves from a general "ask a question" or "casual conversation" type of subverse? Or are we distinguished enough as it is?

This is a discussion for all of us to have. What is next for The Dinner Table? Where do we go from here?

The Dinner Table is committed to being open, honest and transparent in terms of its operation. We value each individual person who dines with us, even if some of them are occasionally dine-and-dash shit-posters. We have developed a reputation as being a place where people can discuss anything they want in an atmosphere that fosters polite, respectful, civil and relaxing conversation.

We are so proud of that, and we hope that you are, too. Let us know what you think about all of this, goats!

Family meeting adjourned.
